subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Can I finish what I was saying before we move on to the next point?
portuguese: Posso acabar o que estava a dizer antes de passarmos ao ponto seguinte?
pronunciationNote: POS-soo ah-kah-BAR oo k esh-TAH-vah ah dee-ZER AN-tush duh pah-SAR-moosh ow PON-too suh-GEEN-tuh
notes: A controlled way to keep your turn in a discussion.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Depois respondo ao que acabou de dizer.
exampleSentences.english: After that I will answer what you just said.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Let me phrase that differently, because I do not think I was clear the first time.
portuguese: Deixe-me formular isso de outra forma, porque acho que não fui claro da primeira vez.
pronunciationNote: DAYSH-muh foor-moo-LAR EE-soo duh OH-trah FOR-mah poor-kuh AH-shoo kuh nawng foo-ee KLAH-roo dah pree-MAY-rah vaysh
notes: A fuller B2 repair phrase for unclear expression.

exampleSentences.portuguese: A ideia principal é outra.
exampleSentences.english: The main idea is different.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I may not have expressed myself well, so let me clarify what I meant.
portuguese: Talvez não me tenha explicado bem, por isso deixe-me esclarecer o que queria dizer.
pronunciationNote: tal-VEZ nawng muh TEN-yah esh-plee-KAH-doo beng poor EE-soo DAYSH-muh esh-klah-reh-SER oo keh kuh-REE-ah dee-ZER
notes: Advanced because it repairs tone and meaning together.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Não estava a criticar a decisão em si.
exampleSentences.english: I was not criticising the decision itself.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I think there may have been a misunderstanding about what was actually agreed.
portuguese: Acho que pode ter havido um mal-entendido sobre o que ficou realmente combinado.
pronunciationNote: AH-shoo kuh POD ter ah-VEE-doo oong mal-en-ten-DEE-doo SOH-br oo keh fee-KOH hee-al-MEN-tuh kohm-bee-NAH-doo
notes: Useful for resolving a disagreement without assigning blame.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Talvez estejamos a partir de ideias diferentes.
exampleSentences.english: Maybe we are starting from different assumptions.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: That is not quite what I had in mind, although I understand why you interpreted it that way.
portuguese: Não era bem isso que eu tinha em mente, embora perceba porque interpretou dessa forma.
pronunciationNote: nawng EH-rah beng EE-soo kuh ew TEE-nyah eng MEN-tuh om-BOH-rah pair-SEH-bah poor-kuh een-ter-pruh-TOH DEH-sah FOR-mah
notes: B2-level because it corrects while acknowledging the other person's interpretation.

exampleSentences.portuguese: A minha intenção era um pouco diferente.
exampleSentences.english: My intention was a little different.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I see what you mean, but I would put it another way so it sounds less direct.
portuguese: Percebo o que quer dizer, mas eu diria de outra forma para soar menos direto.
pronunciationNote: pair-SEH-boo oo keh ker dee-ZER mash ew dee-REE-ah duh OH-trah FOR-mah PAH-rah SOH-ar MEH-noosh dee-REH-too
notes: Advanced because it discusses tone, not just meaning.

exampleSentences.portuguese: A frase está correta, mas o tom pode ser demasiado forte.
exampleSentences.english: The sentence is correct, but the tone may be too strong.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I agree up to a point, but I think the situation is more complicated than that.
portuguese: Concordo até certo ponto, mas acho que a situação é mais complicada do que isso.
pronunciationNote: kohn-KOR-doo ah-TEH SER-too PON-too mash AH-shoo kuh ah see-too-ah-SAWNG eh mysh kohm-plee-KAH-dah doo kuh EE-soo
notes: A full B2 phrase for partial agreement.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Há outros fatores que também contam.
exampleSentences.english: There are other factors that also matter.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I would not put it quite like that, because it could easily be misunderstood.
portuguese: Eu não diria isso exatamente dessa forma, porque podia ser facilmente mal interpretado.
pronunciationNote: ew nawng dee-REE-ah EE-soo egz-ah-tah-MEN-tuh DEH-sah FOR-mah poor-kuh poo-DEE-ah ser fah-seel-MEN-tuh mal een-ter-pruh-TAH-doo
notes: Useful when discussing phrasing, tone, or wording.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Talvez seja melhor usar uma frase mais neutra.
exampleSentences.english: Maybe it is better to use a more neutral phrase.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I take your point, although I see the situation from a slightly different angle.
portuguese: Percebo o seu ponto, embora veja a situação de um ângulo ligeiramente diferente.
pronunciationNote: pair-SEH-boo oo sew PON-too om-BOH-rah VAY-zhah ah see-too-ah-SAWNG duh oong AN-goo-loo lee-zhay-rah-MEN-tuh dee-fuh-REN-tuh
notes: A respectful way to disagree without dismissing the other person.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Acho que estamos a dar peso a aspetos diferentes.
exampleSentences.english: I think we are giving weight to different aspects.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: To be fair, I had not thought of it from that perspective before.
portuguese: Para ser justo, nunca tinha pensado nisso dessa perspetiva.
pronunciationNote: PAH-rah ser ZHOOSH-too NOON-kah TEE-nyah pen-SAH-doo NEE-soo DEH-sah per-shpeh-TEE-vah
notes: Use justa if the speaker is female.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Isso muda um pouco a forma como vejo o assunto.
exampleSentences.english: That changes a little how I see the subject.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: That raises another question, which is whether we are solving the right problem.
portuguese: Isso levanta outra questão, que é saber se estamos a resolver o problema certo.
pronunciationNote: EE-soo luh-VAN-tah OH-trah kesh-TAWNG kuh eh sah-BER suh esh-TAH-moosh ah heh-zol-VER oo proo-BLEH-mah SER-too
notes: Useful for steering deeper discussion.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Talvez estejamos demasiado focados nos detalhes.
exampleSentences.english: Maybe we are too focused on the details.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Before we move on, there is something I would like to clarify.
portuguese: Antes de avançarmos, há uma coisa que gostava de esclarecer.
pronunciationNote: AN-tush duh ah-van-SAR-moosh ah OO-mah KOY-zah kuh goosh-TAH-vah duh esh-klah-reh-SER
notes: Formal enough for work, still natural in conversation.

exampleSentences.portuguese: É uma questão pequena, mas pode evitar confusões.
exampleSentences.english: It is a small question, but it may avoid confusion.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I do not want to sound rude, but I think there is a problem with that assumption.
portuguese: Não quero parecer mal-educado, mas acho que há um problema com esse pressuposto.
pronunciationNote: nawng KEH-roo pah-reh-SER mal-eh-doo-KAH-doo mash AH-shoo kuh ah oong proo-BLEH-mah kohng EH-suh pruh-soo-POOSH-too
notes: Use mal-educada if the speaker is female.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Talvez devêssemos confirmar isso primeiro.
exampleSentences.english: Maybe we should confirm that first.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I do not want to put you on the spot, so we can talk about this later if you prefer.
portuguese: Não quero pô-lo numa situação desconfortável, por isso podemos falar disto mais tarde se preferir.
pronunciationNote: nawng KEH-roo POH-loo NOO-mah see-too-ah-SAWNG desh-kohn-for-TAH-vel poor EE-soo poo-DEH-moosh fah-LAR DEESH-too mysh TAR-duh suh pruh-fuh-REER
notes: Use pô-la if referring formally to a female person.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Não precisa de responder agora.
exampleSentences.english: You do not need to answer now.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: If it is not too much trouble, could you send me that in writing as well?
portuguese: Se não for muito incómodo, podia enviar-me isso também por escrito?
pronunciationNote: suh nawng for MOOY-too een-KOH-moo-doo poo-DEE-ah en-vee-AR-muh EE-soo tam-BAYNG poor esh-KREE-too
notes: A realistic support request for complex information.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Assim consigo confirmar tudo com calma.
exampleSentences.english: That way I can confirm everything calmly.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: If you do not mind me asking, how did you come to that conclusion?
portuguese: Se não se importa que pergunte, como chegou a essa conclusão?
pronunciationNote: suh nawng suh eem-POR-tah kuh pair-GOON-tuh KOH-moo shuh-GOH ah EH-sah kohn-kloo-ZAWNG
notes: A tactful way to ask for reasoning.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Queria perceber melhor o seu raciocínio.
exampleSentences.english: I wanted to understand your reasoning better.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I would rather not go into detail about that here, if you do not mind.
portuguese: Preferia não entrar em detalhes sobre isso aqui, se não se importa.
pronunciationNote: pruh-fuh-REE-ah nawng en-TRAR eng duh-TAL-yush SOH-br EE-soo ah-KEE suh nawng suh eem-POR-tah
notes: A clean way to protect privacy or avoid a sensitive topic.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Podemos falar disso noutra altura.
exampleSentences.english: We can talk about that another time.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: On that subject, I would prefer to leave it there for now.
portuguese: Sobre esse assunto, preferia ficar por aqui por agora.
pronunciationNote: SOH-br EH-suh ah-SOON-too pruh-fuh-REE-ah fee-KAR poor ah-KEE poor ah-GOH-rah
notes: A polite boundary phrase for ending a line of discussion.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Não acho que seja útil continuar.
exampleSentences.english: I do not think it is useful to continue.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Can we set that aside for now and come back to the main point?
portuguese: Podemos deixar isso de lado por agora e voltar ao ponto principal?
pronunciationNote: poo-DEH-moosh day-SHAR EE-soo duh LAH-doo poor ah-GOH-rah ee vol-TAR ow PON-too preen-see-PAL
notes: Useful in meetings, planning, or complex discussions.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Senão vamos perder muito tempo.
exampleSentences.english: Otherwise we are going to lose a lot of time.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I think we are talking about slightly different things, which may be why we disagree.
portuguese: Acho que estamos a falar de coisas ligeiramente diferentes, e talvez seja por isso que discordamos.
pronunciationNote: AH-shoo kuh esh-TAH-moosh ah fah-LAR duh KOY-zash lee-zhay-rah-MEN-tuh dee-fuh-REN-tush ee tal-VEZ SAY-zhah poor EE-soo kuh deesh-kor-DAH-moosh
notes: Advanced because it reframes disagreement as a misunderstanding.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Eu estou a falar do processo, não do resultado.
exampleSentences.english: I am talking about the process, not the result.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: That might be a matter of interpretation rather than a simple mistake.
portuguese: Isso pode ser uma questão de interpretação, mais do que um simples erro.
pronunciationNote: EE-soo POD ser OO-mah kesh-TAWNG duh een-ter-pruh-tah-SAWNG mysh doo kuh oong SEEM-plush EH-roo
notes: Useful for softening correction or disagreement.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Depende muito do contexto.
exampleSentences.english: It depends a lot on the context.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I would need more context to answer properly, otherwise I might give you the wrong impression.
portuguese: Precisava de mais contexto para responder bem, caso contrário podia dar-lhe uma ideia errada.
pronunciationNote: pruh-see-ZAH-vah duh mysh kohn-TESH-too PAH-rah resh-pon-DER beng KAH-zoo kohn-TRAH-ree-oo poo-DEE-ah DAR-lyuh OO-mah ee-DAY-ah eh-HAH-dah
notes: A polished way to avoid over-answering.

exampleSentences.portuguese: A resposta depende muito dos detalhes.
exampleSentences.english: The answer depends a lot on the details.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: It depends what you mean by that, because the word can be used in different ways.
portuguese: Depende do que quer dizer com isso, porque a palavra pode ser usada de formas diferentes.
pronunciationNote: duh-PEN-duh doo kuh ker dee-ZER kohng EE-soo poor-kuh ah pah-LAH-vrah POD ser oo-ZAH-dah duh FOR-mash dee-fuh-REN-tush
notes: Good for discussing meaning and nuance.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Pode dar-me um exemplo concreto?
exampleSentences.english: Can you give me a concrete example?

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Can you be more specific about which part you disagree with?
portuguese: Pode ser mais específico sobre a parte com que discorda?
pronunciationNote: POD ser mysh esh-peh-SEE-fee-koo SOH-br ah PAR-tuh kohng keh deesh-KOR-dah
notes: Use específica if referring to a female person or feminine noun.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Assim é mais fácil responder.
exampleSentences.english: That way it is easier to answer.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I do not want to overstate it, but I think this detail makes a real difference.
portuguese: Não quero exagerar, mas acho que este detalhe faz uma diferença real.
pronunciationNote: nawng KEH-roo egz-ah-zhuh-RAR mash AH-shoo kuh ESH-tuh duh-TAL-yuh faz OO-mah dee-fuh-REN-sah hee-AL
notes: Balances caution with emphasis.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Sem isso, a situação muda bastante.
exampleSentences.english: Without that, the situation changes quite a lot.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I understand the criticism, but I would not go as far as saying it was a failure.
portuguese: Percebo a crítica, mas eu não iria tão longe como dizer que foi um fracasso.
pronunciationNote: pair-SEH-boo ah KREE-tee-kah mash ew nawng ee-REE-ah tawng LON-zhuh KOH-moo dee-ZER kuh foy oong frah-KAH-soo
notes: A complete B2 disagreement phrase with nuance.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Acho que houve problemas, mas também houve aspetos positivos.
exampleSentences.english: I think there were problems, but there were also positive aspects.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: There may be a simpler and more natural way to say that in Portuguese.
portuguese: Talvez haja uma forma mais simples e mais natural de dizer isso em português.
pronunciationNote: tal-VEZ AH-zhah OO-mah FOR-mah mysh SEEM-plush ee mysh nah-too-RAL duh dee-ZER EE-soo eng poor-too-GAYSH
notes: A useful phrase for discussing idiomatic language.

exampleSentences.portuguese: A tradução literal funciona, mas não soa muito bem.
exampleSentences.english: The literal translation works, but it does not sound very good.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: The sentence is correct, but it sounds a bit too direct for this context.
portuguese: A frase está correta, mas soa um pouco direto demais para este contexto.
pronunciationNote: ah FRAH-zuh shTAH koo-REH-tah mash SOH-ah oong POH-koo dee-REH-too duh-MYSH PAH-rah ESH-tuh kohn-TESH-too
notes: Advanced because it separates grammar from pragmatic tone.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Eu usaria uma formulação mais suave.
exampleSentences.english: I would use a softer wording.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: Thanks for bearing with me; I know it takes me a little longer to explain things in Portuguese.
portuguese: Obrigado pela paciência; sei que demoro um pouco mais a explicar as coisas em português.
pronunciationNote: oh-bree-GAH-doo PEH-lah pah-see-EN-see-ah say kuh duh-MOH-roo oong POH-koo mysh ah esh-plee-KAR ash KOY-zash eng poor-too-GAYSH
notes: Use obrigada if the speaker is female.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Mas quero continuar a praticar.
exampleSentences.english: But I want to keep practising.

subject: Everyday Conversation Tools
english: I can see both sides of the argument, but I am leaning towards the second option.
portuguese: Consigo ver os dois lados da questão, mas estou mais inclinado para a segunda opção.
pronunciationNote: kohn-SEE-goo ver oosh doysh LAH-doosh dah kesh-TAWNG mash esh-TOH mysh een-klee-NAH-doo PAH-rah ah suh-GOON-dah op-SAWNG
notes: Use inclinada if the speaker is female.

exampleSentences.portuguese: Parece-me a solução mais prática.
exampleSentences.english: It seems to me the most practical solution.
